available-to-promise.title: Available to promise - Wikipedia
available-to-promise.notes: Available to promise (ATP) is a business function that answers a customer's order inquiry by checking whether resources exist to meet it. It establishes how much of a requested product can be supplied and by when, which supports order promising and fulfilment and keeps customer demand aligned with production plans. The check is made before a delivery commitment is given. ATP usually comes built into enterprise management software, although companies often have to tailor it to their own processes. It can run in real time, handling each order as it arrives, or in batch mode, where orders gathered over a period are evaluated together. The article separates push and pull approaches. Push-based ATP relies on demand forecasts, classically figures derived from the master production schedule, and suffers when forecasts are wrong. In this approach gross ATP is the total supply on hand, while net ATP is what is left once existing customer commitments are deducted. Pull-based ATP allocates resources dynamically as real orders come in, balancing forecast-driven replenishment against order-driven consumption. Because it commits resources order by order, it can give myopic results, meaning decisions that look sensible locally but are not optimal overall.

aws-direct-connect.title: What is AWS Direct Connect? - AWS Direct Connect User Guide
aws-direct-connect.notes: AWS Direct Connect links an organization's own network to AWS through a dedicated fibre-optic connection at a Direct Connect location, so traffic bypasses internet service providers on its path. The customer's router connects to a Direct Connect router, and virtual interfaces (VIFs) are created over that link to reach AWS services. Three VIF types exist: a private VIF reaches resources in Amazon VPCs by private IP address and can attach to one VPC or to a Direct Connect gateway spanning several VPCs and accounts; a public VIF reaches AWS public services such as Amazon S3 through public IP addresses; and a transit VIF reaches one or more Transit Gateways associated with a Direct Connect gateway. To use the service, a network must be colocated at a Direct Connect location, go through an AWS Partner Network partner, or use an independent service provider. Equipment needs single-mode fibre with a supported transceiver, 802.1Q VLAN support along the whole path, and BGP with MD5 authentication; BFD is optional for faster failure detection. Both IPv4 and IPv6 are supported. Billing has two parts: port-hour charges that depend on capacity and connection type, plus outbound data transfer. Quotas cap the number of VIFs and gateway associations.

azure-ai-content-safety.title: What is Azure AI Content Safety? - Microsoft Learn
azure-ai-content-safety.notes: Azure AI Content Safety is a Microsoft AI service that detects harmful content in both user-generated and AI-generated material. It offers text and image APIs, and a web tool called Content Safety Studio lets teams try content, configure filters and design moderation workflows without training their own models. The Analyze Text and Analyze Image APIs scan for sexual content, violence, hate and self-harm, each reported with several severity levels. Further AI-safety features include Prompt Shields, which detects attacks on language models, groundedness detection that checks whether a response matches its source material (preview), and protected material detection for known copyrighted text. Custom categories let customers define their own harmful-content patterns (preview). Blocklists are supported, including Microsoft's built-in profanity lists, and access can use Microsoft Entra ID or managed identities. Two pricing tiers exist, F0 and S0. The service cannot detect illegal child exploitation imagery. Protected material, groundedness and standard custom categories support English only; other models are mainly tested in eight languages.

azure-autoscale.title: Overview of autoscale in Azure - Azure Monitor - Microsoft Learn
azure-autoscale.notes: Azure Monitor autoscale automatically adds or removes resource instances to match application load, keeping performance steady while cutting cost when demand falls. It scales horizontally only: it changes the number of instances, for example virtual machines in a scale set, and cannot give existing instances more CPU or memory. Configuration is built from scale conditions, called profiles in JSON and the CLI. Each condition defines a minimum, maximum and default instance count so scaling stays within bounds, and holds rules plus a schedule. Rules can be metric-based, using values such as CPU usage, queue length or custom Application Insights metrics, or time-based. Autoscale scales out when any rule is met but scales in only when all scale-in rules are met. A profile can contain up to 10 rules and one setting up to 20 profiles. Schedules let different conditions apply at different hours or weekdays. When rules fire, autoscale can send email or call webhooks that start runbooks, functions or logic apps. Predictive autoscale applies machine learning to historical CPU patterns to forecast cyclical load on Virtual Machine Scale Sets and add capacity ahead of demand. Availability sets are a legacy option with limited support, and Microsoft recommends migrating to scale sets.

azure-management-group.title: Organize your resources with management groups - Microsoft Learn
azure-management-group.notes: Azure management groups are a governance scope that sits above subscriptions. Policy and access assignments made on a management group pass down by inheritance to its child management groups, subscriptions and resources. The article's example is a policy limiting VM regions on a group called Corp, which then applies to every subscription beneath it, and resource owners cannot override it. All subscriptions in one group must trust the same Microsoft Entra tenant. Management groups also allow a single role assignment to cover many subscriptions instead of scripting access one by one. Each directory has exactly one hierarchy, starting at a built-in root management group that all other groups and subscriptions fold into, so anything assigned there applies to the entire directory. By default it is named Tenant root group, its ID equals the tenant ID, and it cannot be moved or deleted. Nobody has access to it by default; Global Administrators must first elevate their access, and the page advises assigning things there only when essential. Stated limits are up to 10,000 management groups per directory and up to six levels of depth, not counting the root or the subscription level. Each management group or subscription has one parent, while a group may have many children.

azure-monitor-agent.title: Azure Monitor Agent overview - Microsoft Learn
azure-monitor-agent.notes: The Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) collects monitoring data from the guest operating system of virtual machines and delivers it to Azure Monitor. Services such as Microsoft Sentinel use that data, and the agent can be installed on VMs in Azure, in other clouds or on premises. It is the supported agent for guest OS data and replaces the legacy Log Analytics agent. What the agent gathers is governed by data collection rules (DCRs), which define what to collect, how to process it and where to send it. The agent fetches its associated DCRs on installation and checks for updates periodically, so configuration stays consistent across large numbers of machines. On Windows it can collect event logs, performance counters, file-based logs and IIS logs; on Linux it collects Syslog, performance data and file-based logs. The main destination is Azure Monitor Logs. The agent is free, but ingestion and storage of the data are billed. The page lists gaps: the VM extension is not supported in air-gapped clouds (the Windows MSI installer is), Microsoft Defender for Cloud does not use AMA and relies on the Defender for Endpoint agent, Update Manager no longer uses agents, and some features are Windows-only. Linux file-based log collection and Windows client OS support exist only with AMA.

azure-rbac.title: What is Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC)? - Microsoft Learn
azure-rbac.notes: Azure role-based access control is an authorization system built on Azure Resource Manager. It governs who can reach Azure resources, what they may do with them, and which areas they can access. Access is granted through a role assignment, which has three parts: a security principal (a user, group, service principal or managed identity), a role definition (a set of permissions such as read, write or delete, available as built-in or custom roles) and a scope. Scope can be a management group, subscription, resource group or single resource. Scopes form a parent-child hierarchy, so a role assigned at a higher level extends to everything below it. Creating a role assignment gives access, and deleting it removes access. Group membership is transitive and overlapping assignments are additive, so a person's effective permissions are the sum of everything assigned to them. The article also describes deny assignments, which block access where they apply, and notes that role assignments can carry conditions. Role data is stored globally, so removing an assignment takes effect everywhere. The feature is included free with an Azure subscription. The overview does not spell out quotas or other numeric limits.

azure-region-pairs.title: Azure region pairs and nonpaired regions - Microsoft Learn
azure-region-pairs.notes: An Azure region pair consists of two regions within the same geography that Microsoft links together. Most pairs are symmetrical, but some are asymmetrical; West US 3, for instance, pairs with East US in one direction only. Many regions have no pair at all and depend on availability zones for redundancy. Pairing gives three benefits. After a geography-wide outage, one region of each pair is prioritised for recovery. Planned platform updates are staggered across a pair so a faulty update does not reach both regions at once. And because most pairs stay inside one geography, data residency requirements are easier to meet. Some services use the pair for geo-redundancy, for example geo-redundant storage replicating data to the paired region. The page is explicit about limits: deploying into a paired region does not by itself make a solution resilient or give automatic failover, so customers still need their own high-availability and disaster recovery plans. Microsoft-managed failover between regions of a pair is reserved for catastrophic situations after repeated failed recovery attempts, and should not be the main disaster recovery strategy.

bill-of-materials.title: Bill of materials - Wikipedia
bill-of-materials.notes: A bill of materials (BOM) lists the raw materials, subassemblies, components and parts needed to build a finished product, together with the quantity of each. A manufacturer may share a BOM with partners or use it inside one plant, and it is often tied to a production order, which reserves components already in stock and requests those that are missing. The BOM is hierarchical, with the finished product at the top and its subassemblies and parts below. A single-level BOM names only the direct components of one assembly, while an indented or multi-level BOM shows every parent-child relationship. Explosion breaks an assembly into its parts, and implosion links parts back up to a major assembly. In process industries the same list is called a formula, recipe or ingredients list. BOMs take different forms for different purposes: an engineering BOM describes the product as designed, a sales BOM as ordered, a manufacturing BOM as built and a service BOM as maintained. Configurable BOMs suit products with many options, such as vehicles or servers. In electronics a BOM lists every component on a printed circuit board, with parts omitted from a variant marked do not populate. Overall it serves as a central reference for design, procurement, production planning and maintenance.

billennium.title: Billennium - IT services company (company website)
billennium.notes: Billennium presents itself on its website as an IT services company that combines AI with skilled IT professionals. The page does not name a headquarters, but it lists offices in Canada, Switzerland, Poland (six locations), India, Malaysia, Germany, the United States and the Netherlands, and stresses its Polish roots through a follow-the-sun support model it says has run for more than 20 years. It offers three service lines: expert staffing, which supplies IT talent to projects; managed services, covering full IT management and implementation; and technology solutions for scalable IT environments. Listed areas of expertise include software development, cloud computing, data and AI, enterprise platforms, integration and automation, and process management with quality assurance. Packaged offers mentioned include an AI governance suite, AI procurement agents, Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption and cloud cost management. Microsoft is named among its technology partners alongside Salesforce, AWS and Snowflake, though the page does not describe the nature or level of the partnership.

botnet.title: Botnet - Wikipedia
botnet.notes: A botnet is a network of internet-connected devices, such as computers, smartphones or Internet of Things gadgets, that have been infected with malware and placed under the control of a third party. Each infected device is called a bot or zombie and is directed remotely by its operator, the bot herder, through command-and-control channels. The architecture has changed over time. Early botnets used a client-server model in which bots contacted IRC channels, websites or domains to receive orders. Newer ones often use peer-to-peer designs in which every infected machine can both relay and receive instructions, so no single server can be shut down to stop the network. Operators also use fast-flux DNS, domain generation algorithms and legitimate services such as GitHub or Tor to hide their control infrastructure. Botnets are used for distributed denial-of-service attacks, spam, credential theft through keystroke logging, credential stuffing, click and ad fraud, phishing and cryptocurrency mining, and operators often rent capacity to others as attack-for-hire. They are illegal in most jurisdictions and prosecuted as hacking or fraud. Authorities and researchers respond with server seizures, domain takedowns and detection tools, as in Europol's Operation Endgame.

bottleneck.title: Bottleneck (production) - Wikipedia
bottleneck.notes: A bottleneck is a step in a chain of processes whose limited capacity reduces the output of the whole chain. The article lists its effects as production stalls, excess supply, customer pressure, lower employee morale, equipment wear, storage costs and longer hours for staff. Bottlenecks can be short-term, such as a skilled worker being briefly absent, or long-term, such as an inefficient machine with a permanent queue, and long-term ones add up to significant slowdowns. Almost every system has some bottleneck, even if minor. They can be located by looking for where work piles up, measuring throughput, checking how fully machines are used and tracking downtime and wait times; a fishbone diagram can help find the cause of a delay. The longest queue does not always mark the bottleneck. Suggested ways to manage one include adding staff, cutting downtime, removing non-value tasks, keeping buffer stock upstream, reducing setup time, cross-training workers, maintaining the constrained equipment and scheduling carefully. The page distinguishes static systems, with no random variation, where the bottleneck is simply the slowest process, from dynamic systems, which always vary.

broken-object-level-authorization.title: API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization - OWASP API Security Top 10
broken-object-level-authorization.notes: Broken object level authorization (BOLA) is the first entry in the 2023 OWASP API Security Top 10. It is a flaw in which the server never verifies that the caller is allowed to act on a particular object. The endpoint itself is normally open to the user, so the weakness lies at the level of the individual object, not the endpoint. APIs often trust identifiers supplied by the client, such as numbers, UUIDs or strings in paths, query strings, headers or request bodies, so an attacker can change an ID to reach another user's data. OWASP calls the issue very common. The page gives three scenarios: a script that varies shop names in a URL to pull sales data from thousands of stores, a vehicle-control API that accepts any vehicle identifier without checking ownership, and a document service that deletes whatever document ID arrives through a GraphQL mutation with no permission check. Impacts include unauthorised data disclosure, data loss, data manipulation and, in some cases, full account takeover. Recommended prevention is to enforce authorisation based on user policies and hierarchy, to check access in every function that uses client input to reach a record, and to prefer random, unpredictable identifiers such as GUIDs.

business-central-agent-designer.title: Envision and prototype custom AI agents using Agent Designer - Business Central release plan
business-central-agent-designer.notes: Agent Designer is an in-product experience in the AI Development Toolkit for Dynamics 365 Business Central. It lets people envision, build and test custom AI agents on the same agent runtime that powers built-in agents such as the Sales Order Agent and Payables Agent. It is aimed at consultants, product owners, developers and power users. An agent's goals and behaviour are written as natural-language instructions, much like prompts for a language model, with a built-in editor for refining and testing them. Each agent is given profiles and permissions that set its access boundaries, every step is logged, and a timeline shows what the agent did and why. Agents can be tried against Business Central data in a low-risk sandbox before moving to production, and definitions can be exported and imported as JSON files to back them up or move them between sandboxes. An agent is started by creating a task, optionally with extra context; built-in triggers for emails, events or schedules are not yet available, though pasting email text into a task simulates one. Execution logs show inputs, reasoning and outputs for tuning instructions. Custom agents consume Copilot credits, bought prepaid or pay-as-you-go.

bystander-effect.title: Bystander effect - Wikipedia
bystander-effect.notes: The bystander effect is a social-psychology theory holding that people are less likely to help a victim when other people are present. It is also called bystander apathy or the Genovese effect. The idea arose in 1964 after the murder of Kitty Genovese in Queens, New York, when a newspaper reported that 37 bystanders saw or heard the attack without helping or calling the police. Later reviews found that account exaggerated, with fewer witnesses and at least one call to the police. Laboratory research began in 1968 with John Darley and Bibb Latane. Participants who were alone generally reacted to an apparent emergency faster and more often than those in groups; in a 1969 study 70 percent of people alone helped a woman who seemed injured, against 40 percent of those paired with a stranger. Darley and Latane explained the effect mainly through diffusion of responsibility: when others are present each person assumes someone else will act. Bystanders also watch the reactions of others to judge whether something is an emergency, and if nobody reacts they may conclude nothing is wrong. A 2011 meta-analysis found the effect weaker in dangerous emergencies.

canary-release.title: CanaryRelease - Martin Fowler
canary-release.notes: Canary release is a technique for lowering the risk of deploying a new software version. Instead of switching every user at once, the new version first goes to a small part of the infrastructure that receives no user traffic. When that looks healthy, a small group of users is routed to it, selected by random sampling, as internal staff or by user profile. As confidence grows, more servers and users move over until everyone is on the new version and the old infrastructure can be retired. If problems show up, traffic is sent back to the old version until the issue is fixed. The practice is also called a phased or incremental rollout. The main benefits are early warning of problems before they reach everyone and a way to test capacity under real production conditions. Because the rollback path is safe, load on the new version can be raised gradually without a separate testing environment. The article lists drawbacks: running several versions at once adds management work, so the number of concurrent versions should stay small; it is harder for software installed on users' own devices, since the vendor cannot control when users upgrade and backends must support old and new clients; and database changes must work with both versions during the rollout.

capa.title: Corrective and preventive action - Wikipedia
capa.notes: CAPA, corrective and preventive action, is a set of process improvements an organisation makes to remove the causes of non-conformities such as product defects, equipment failures, quality-system gaps or misread work instructions. Each CAPA follows a root cause analysis, often using methods such as the 5 Whys or an Ishikawa diagram, and is designed by a team that includes quality staff and the people who saw the problem. Corrective action deals with a problem that has already occurred so that it does not recur, while preventive action anticipates potential problems, usually through risk analysis, and stops them before they happen. The work follows a plan-do-check-act cycle: investigate causes, implement actions, review whether they worked and take further steps if needed. An investigation may conclude that no action is necessary or only a simple fix. Problems can surface through customer complaints, internal or third-party audits, statistical process control trends, staff suggestions and management reviews. CAPA is required in medical device and pharmaceutical manufacturing; under FDA rule 21 CFR 820.100, mishandling it can make a product adulterated or substandard. It also forms part of good manufacturing practice, HACCP and ISO standards.

capable-to-promise.title: Capable-to-promise, an overview - Infor LN documentation
capable-to-promise.notes: This Infor LN documentation page introduces capable-to-promise (CTP) as a group of order-promising techniques. They help answer sales questions such as whether a quantity of an item can be delivered by a given date, how soon a quantity could arrive, or how much can ship before a month ends. CTP spans a range of methods, from basic available-to-promise (ATP) checks on standard items to more advanced approaches, and each draws on a different source of availability. Standard ATP uses supply that is already planned for the product. Capacity CTP looks at capacity that could be converted into deliverable supply. Component CTP uses the ATP of components linked to the product. Channel ATP considers the maximum volume that can be sold through a particular channel, and family CTP supports long-term promising at product-family level. The software also supports CTP for customised items. The page identifies the kinds of information consulted when answering a promise request, but it does not walk through how a delivery date is calculated. One concrete fact concerns multisite setups: when multisite functionality is active, CTP and ATP calculations run per planning cluster, and if a cluster is linked to several sites the checks use the combined supply across those sites.

capacity-profile.title: Create and manage capacity profiles - Dynamics 365 Customer Service
capacity-profile.notes: Capacity profiles in Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Contact Center define how much work a service representative can take on. Administrators create profiles, assign them to representatives and use them in workstreams to route work items. Each profile sets a work item limit, the number of work units a representative may be assigned. A reset frequency decides when consumption resets, either immediately or at the end of the shift, and it cannot be changed later without recreating the profile. Assignment blocking stops new work once the limit is reached and switches the representative's presence to Busy-DND. Limits can be customised per representative, higher or lower than the profile default, in the admin center or through the msdyn_maxunits field; custom limits apply only to new assignments and can take up to 15 minutes to sync. A representative can hold several profiles, and assignment requires capacity in all attached profiles. A workstream sets a default profile, and classification rules can add more. Capacity is released when conversations end or cases are resolved, while other records such as emails must be deactivated or have the representative removed from the Worked By field.

capture-the-flag.title: Capture the flag - Wikipedia
capture-the-flag.notes: Capture the flag is a traditional outdoor game in which two teams each guard a flag in their own territory. Players try to sneak into the opposing side, seize its flag and carry it home without being tagged. They are safe on their own side but vulnerable once they cross into enemy territory. Rules vary: a tagged player may be sent to a jail, returned to base, frozen in place or removed from the game, and may be freed after a set time or by a teammate. Flag rules differ too; a tagged carrier's flag may return to its start or stay where it was lost, and in many versions it may be tossed to a teammate as long as it does not touch the ground. Variants include one-flag games with separate offensive and defensive teams, multi-flag games where a team wins only after taking all the flags, bandanna games where players pull a cloth from an opponent's pocket instead of tagging, urban indoor versions with walls, and airsoft, paintball or Nerf versions that usually lack territories. The game has roots in 19th-century European play, with rules appearing in an 1860 German gymnastics manual as Fahnenbarlauf, followed by English descriptions in Baden-Powell's Scouting for Boys (1908) and a 1920 Boy Scouts of America handbook.

carbon-removal.title: Carbon dioxide removal - Wikipedia
carbon-removal.notes: Carbon dioxide removal (CDR), also called carbon removal, greenhouse gas removal or negative emissions, is the deliberate removal of CO2 from the atmosphere and its durable storage in geological, land or ocean reservoirs, or in products. Methods fall into two groups. Land-based approaches include planting forests, improving soil carbon through farming, bioenergy combined with carbon capture, and direct air capture with storage. Ocean and water-based approaches include ocean fertilisation, ocean alkalinity enhancement, wetland restoration and blue carbon management. Biological stores such as forests are considered volatile because fire, disease or policy shifts can release the carbon again, whereas geological and mineral storage can last far longer. According to the article, CDR currently removes about 2 gigatons of CO2 per year, roughly 4 percent of annual human greenhouse gas emissions, mostly through reforestation, and studies suggest methods deployable today could reach around 10 gigatons per year, although measuring removals precisely is difficult. CDR is different from carbon capture and storage at point sources such as power plants, which cuts new emissions but does not lower CO2 already in the air.

cash-flow-forecasting.title: Cash flow forecasting - Wikipedia
cash-flow-forecasting.notes: Cash flow forecasting estimates a company's future cash position and wider financial health over a chosen period. It is a key tool for large corporations and small businesses alike, helping managers spot shortfalls early so they can pay suppliers and staff and avoid insolvency. How often to forecast depends on the business, its industry and regulation; forecasts may become daily in a crisis, and banks may require them when a loan is involved. In corporate finance the forecast models future liquidity: short-term work supports working capital management, while longer-term work supports asset and liability management. The focus is often the treasury position, which combines cash, short-term investments and short-term debt, and the projections also inform valuation, budgeting and capital structure decisions. The article describes four main methods. The direct method lists expected receipts and payments and suits about 30 days ahead. Three indirect methods build from projected income statements and balance sheets: the adjusted net income method, the pro-forma balance sheet method and the accrual reversal method.

chief-information-security-officer.title: Chief information security officer - Wikipedia
chief-information-security-officer.notes: A chief information security officer (CISO) is a senior executive who sets the strategy and program for protecting an organisation's information and technology. The CISO leads work to reduce IT and information risk, oversees security tools and policies, and ensures compliance with rules such as GDPR, PCI DSS and FISMA, which often includes protecting company and customer data and supporting certifications like ISO/IEC 27001. Typical responsibilities include incident response, cybersecurity, disaster recovery, identity and access management, privacy, risk management and security operations. Modern CISOs also advise executives and boards on cyber risk, align security spending with business goals and monitor third-party and supply-chain exposure. Reporting lines have shifted: CISOs once often reported to the chief information officer, but by 2019 only 24 percent did so, while 40 percent reported to the CEO and 27 percent to the board; moving away from IT reporting helps avoid conflicts of interest. The role emerged in the mid-1990s, and Steven Katz, appointed at Citicorp in 1995, is regarded as the first CISO. About 85 percent of businesses had a CISO or equivalent by 2018, and US federal law requires agencies to have a senior information security officer.

child-flows.title: Create child flows - Power Automate - Microsoft Learn
child-flows.notes: Child flows let a large Power Automate flow be split into smaller, reusable pieces. A parent flow, which can have any trigger, calls a child flow containing a set of steps. This keeps flows with dozens or hundreds of actions easier to navigate and maintain and lets the same logic be reused in several places. A child flow is built inside a solution as an instant cloud flow with the Manually trigger a flow trigger. It defines inputs, for example a contact name and email, that the parent passes in, and ends with a Respond to a Power App or flow action, or a Response action, that returns outputs. If it uses connections other than built-in actions or the Dataverse connector, its run-only user setting must use embedded connections, because connections supplied by the parent are not supported. In the parent, the Run a Child Flow action from the Flows connector, under the Built-in tab, selects the child; the parent waits for it to finish and can use its outputs. Parent and child should sit in the same solution, since importing a flow into a solution can produce unexpected results. A child flow does not inherit Process license capacity from its parent; both must be added to the same flow group, and each counts toward the 25-flow limit.

ci-cd.title: CI/CD - Wikipedia
ci-cd.notes: CI/CD combines continuous integration (CI), continuous delivery (CD) and, less often, continuous deployment; it is sometimes called continuous development. Continuous integration means developers frequently merge small changes into a main branch. Continuous delivery means producing software in short, rapid cycles so that it can be released at any time through a simple, repeatable process. Continuous deployment means new functionality is rolled out automatically. When these stages run in sequence they form a CI/CD pipeline. The practice bridges development and operations teams by automating how applications are built, tested and deployed: automated tests check functionality and automated services deliver the finished software to users. The stated goals are to find defects earlier, raise productivity and speed up releases. This contrasts with older methods that batched many updates into one large integration before deployment. Modern DevOps includes continuous development, testing, integration, deployment and monitoring, and the pipeline is central to it. The page also lists practices that improve pipeline productivity, especially in cloud environments. Small teams often work best with one repository and one pipeline, while larger organisations may split them by team or service.

cidr.title: Classless Inter-Domain Routing - Wikipedia
cidr.notes: Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) is a method for allocating IP addresses and routing traffic between networks. The IETF introduced it in 1993 through RFC 1518 and RFC 1519, and it was updated in RFC 4632 in 2006. Its goals were to slow the growth of Internet routing tables and to delay exhaustion of IPv4 addresses. The older classful system offered only three fixed network sizes, Classes A, B and C, so organisations often received far more addresses than they needed or far too few, wasting space and producing many scattered routes. CIDR removes those fixed classes: providers can assign blocks of any size that match real needs, and contiguous blocks can be combined into a single larger route entry, which shrinks global routing tables. CIDR notation pairs an address with a prefix length after a slash, as in 192.0.2.0/24. The prefix length is the number of leading bits identifying the network, and a block holds 2 raised to the power of (total address bits minus prefix length) addresses, so an IPv4 /29 contains 8 addresses. The same notation applies to IPv6, where prefixes range from 0 to 128 and /64 is the standard subnet size. Phil Karn is credited with inventing the notation in the 1980s.

closed-loop-production-scheduling.title: What is real-time production rescheduling and how does it work? - Delfoi
closed-loop-production-scheduling.notes: This article from a production-scheduling software vendor describes real-time rescheduling as a way to update a production plan as soon as something unexpected happens, instead of waiting for the next daily or weekly planning cycle. Triggers include machine breakdowns, material shortages, absent operators, quality failures and rush orders. Small events can often be absorbed by existing buffers, but a breakdown on a bottleneck machine can affect many downstream orders. The process runs as a closed loop of four steps: detect the disruption, evaluate its impact, replan the schedule within resource and due-date constraints, and communicate the update to everyone who needs it. A cycle can take seconds or minutes. Because jobs share resources, changing one job shifts the timing of others, so the system should make these knock-on effects visible. Shop-floor feedback is central: the article names actual production progress, compared with what the plan assumed, as the most important data stream, with machine status, material availability and order priorities also feeding the loop. It warns that a reschedule is only as good as its input data, and that manufacturers without reliable machine data, or who rely on spreadsheets, should fix those gaps first.

cloud-egress.title: What are data egress fees? - Cloudflare Learning Center
cloud-egress.notes: Data egress fees are charges that cloud providers impose for moving data out of their storage or network. They are also called bandwidth or data transfer fees and are billed separately from storage and compute. The article argues that part of the reason providers charge them is that they act as a kind of tax on leaving the provider's ecosystem; the fees tend to grow as a company relies more on the cloud and can contribute to vendor lock-in. Pricing varies widely: Amazon Web Services, for example, charges up to about 0.09 US dollars per gigabyte transferred out of its storage, and real costs are hard to predict because they depend on subscription tier, monthly volume, region and destination. Ingress, data entering a cloud, is typically free, whereas egress is usually billed once it exceeds a provider's free tier. Common egress scenarios include serving content to users, connecting applications, downloading data locally and moving data to another cloud. Organisations may still move data across clouds for disaster recovery, performance or hybrid strategies.

cloud-kerberos-trust.title: Cloud Kerberos trust deployment - Windows Hello for Business - Microsoft Learn
cloud-kerberos-trust.notes: Cloud Kerberos trust is a Windows Hello for Business trust model for hybrid environments in which Active Directory identities are synchronised to Microsoft Entra ID. It authenticates users to Active Directory with keys, so no certificates need to be issued, and Microsoft recommends it for environments that do not require certificate authentication. Enabling Microsoft Entra Kerberos creates an AzureADKerberos computer object in the domain, which Microsoft Entra ID uses to produce Kerberos ticket-granting tickets for that domain. Users who belong, directly or indirectly, to privileged built-in groups cannot use the trust, and the default Password Replication Policy blocks high-privilege accounts; Microsoft advises against relaxing that policy. Requirements include Microsoft Entra Kerberos already deployed for the domain (true if on-premises single sign-on for security keys exists), the policies Use Windows Hello for Business and Use cloud trust for on-premises authentication enabled, optionally Require security device, the Use certificate for on-premises authentication policy left unconfigured because certificate trust takes precedence, and enough read-write domain controllers in each site where users sign in.

cmmc.title: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification - Wikipedia
cmmc.notes: The Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) is a US Department of Defense framework and certification program that verifies whether defence contractors protect sensitive government information, namely controlled unclassified information (CUI) and federal contract information (FCI), on their systems. It builds mainly on NIST SP 800-171, and some contracts add requirements from SP 800-172. The model has three levels. Level 1 covers 14 basic practices for protecting FCI and is verified through an annual self-assessment. Level 2 covers 110 practices aligned with NIST SP 800-171 for protecting CUI, with third-party assessments every three years for critical programs. Level 3 adds a subset of SP 800-172 requirements to Level 2 and involves government-led assessments every three years. Contractors were already self-assessing against NIST SP 800-171 after DFARS rules took effect in 2016 and 2017. The Department of Defense announced CMMC in 2019 after supply-chain breaches, a streamlined CMMC 2.0 followed in November 2021, and a proposed rule came in December 2023. The page reports that the 48 CFR rule cleared review in August 2025 and that in July 2026 the Pentagon temporarily paused Phase 2, with a task force to review the program. Enforcement awaits final rulemaking.

cmms.title: Computerized maintenance management system - Wikipedia
cmms.notes: A computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) is software that stores information about an organisation's maintenance activities in a computer database. Maintenance staff use the data to work more efficiently; for example, they can see which machines need servicing and which storerooms hold the parts they need. Managers use it to make better-informed decisions, such as comparing the cost of repairing equipment after a breakdown with the cost of preventive upkeep, which can help allocate resources more wisely. The article also says the data can help demonstrate that a facility meets regulatory requirements. Without software, analysing what happens in a facility's maintenance operations takes a great deal of time and effort, and a CMMS simplifies this by keeping records and tracking assigned and completed tasks in a timely and cost-effective way. In practice that means it holds work orders and maintenance history and supports organising and documenting maintenance work. The entry itself is short and is supported by four book references, from 1994 to 2010, and it carries a note that it needs additional citations, so some statements are not fully sourced.

code-interpreter.title: Code Interpreter tool for Foundry agents - Microsoft Learn
code-interpreter.notes: Code Interpreter lets a Microsoft Foundry agent write and run Python to analyse data, generate charts, solve maths problems and iterate on results. The page recommends adding it through a toolbox so the tool can be reused across agents with centralised credentials, versioning and policy. Code runs in a Microsoft-managed sandbox built on dynamic sessions in Azure Container Apps, with each session isolated by a Hyper-V boundary. The sandbox runs in the same region as the project, cannot make outbound network requests and does not inherit the agent's subnet configuration. Containers are not isolated per agent or user within a project, so the page advises treating container IDs as sensitive and not sharing containers across trust boundaries. Supported inputs include CSV, JSON, XML, PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, TXT, Markdown, source code, images (PNG, JPEG, GIF) and ZIP or TAR archives, uploaded with the purpose set to assistants. Generated files such as charts return as container file citation annotations and can be downloaded. Sessions stay active for up to one hour with a 30-minute idle timeout, and the package set is fixed, so custom packages need the separate custom code interpreter tool.

common-vulnerabilities-and-exposures.title: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures - Wikipedia
common-vulnerabilities-and-exposures.notes: CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) is a reference system that gives publicly known information-security vulnerabilities standard identifiers. The US government funds it and MITRE, operating a federally funded research center, maintains it; it went public in September 1999. Each ID follows the pattern CVE-year-number, starting with four digits and growing longer only when a year needs more entries, and a 2015 syntax change lifted the earlier limit of 9,999 per year. Every ID begins as reserved and is published once accepted as a real vulnerability, while entries that do not qualify can be rejected. The old CAN prefix for candidates was retired in 2005. IDs are issued by CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs): MITRE is the primary CNA, software vendors such as Microsoft, Oracle, HP and Red Hat issue IDs for their own products, and third-party coordinators like CERT/CC cover products without a CNA. Vendors have wide discretion over whether to assign an ID, which has drawn criticism and led to the 2023 !CVE project tracking vendor-rejected vulnerabilities. The CVE list feeds the US National Vulnerability Database, which builds on CVE IDs.

compliance-manager-assessment.title: Build and manage assessments in Compliance Manager - Microsoft Purview
compliance-manager-assessment.notes: Compliance Manager assessments help an organisation measure its compliance with industry and regional regulations and track the work needed to meet them. Each assessment is built from a regulatory template that supplies controls and improvement actions, and one assessment can cover several services, such as Microsoft 365 and non-Microsoft clouds. Assessments are organised into groups, and improvement actions can be shared across the assessments of a group. Progress is measured by the share of controls tested, and each control carries a status such as Passed, Failed, In progress or Out of scope. Points are earned by completing improvement actions, and a default Data Protection Baseline assessment provides the initial score; the Microsoft 365 Copilot baseline and AI regulation templates add further options. More than 360 regulatory templates are available, though which ones can be used depends on licensing, and custom assessments are in preview. When Microsoft or the organisation updates a template, the change can be accepted or deferred. Assessment details can be exported to Excel as a snapshot for auditors or stakeholders.

connected-agents.title: Add other agents - Microsoft Copilot Studio - Microsoft Learn
connected-agents.notes: This page explains how to extend a Copilot Studio agent, called the main agent, by adding other agents that take over interactions or respond to triggers. The options are child agents built inside the main agent, other Copilot Studio agents in the same environment (connected agents), and external agents, including A2A agents, Microsoft Foundry, Fabric Data and Microsoft 365 Agents SDK agents, the last three in preview. The main agent can use them in two ways: its orchestration chooses one automatically based on the agents' names and descriptions, or a topic explicitly redirects to an agent and then resumes afterwards. Authors can also reference agents in the Instructions field by typing a slash. On the Agents page an agent can be switched off with the Enabled toggle, a child agent can be deleted and a connected agent disconnected. Connected agents follow the main agent's Use general knowledge setting, and if one produces an ungrounded response while Allow ungrounded responses is off, that response is discarded. The page does not describe authentication.

connection-references.title: Use a connection reference in a solution - Power Apps - Microsoft Learn
connection-references.notes: A connection reference is a solution component that points to a connection for a particular connector. A connection holds the authentication credentials for a connector, such as OAuth credentials for SharePoint. Solution-aware canvas apps and flows bind to the connection reference and not to the connection itself, which lets them move between environments: when a solution is imported, a connection is supplied for each reference, and flows that use them can be switched on automatically afterwards. To change the connection an app or flow uses, the reference is edited in the solution instead of the app or flow. A reference can be created manually in solution explorer, during solution import, or implicitly while building apps and flows inside a solution. Flows use references for all connectors, whereas canvas apps use them only for non-OAuth connections. Flows outside a solution can be upgraded by reimporting an unmanaged export or with the flow checker action Use connection references, while canvas apps must have the connection removed and added again. Whoever turns on a flow must own or be allowed to use all its connections, so connections are often shared with Can use permission.

content-assembly.title: Overview of content assembly - SharePoint Premium - Microsoft Learn
content-assembly.notes: Content assembly is a Microsoft 365 feature that automatically generates standard, repetitive business documents such as contracts, statements of work, service agreements and consent letters, making document creation faster, more consistent and less error-prone. A modern template is created by uploading an existing Word document and adding fields to the sections that change. Those fields can be linked to SharePoint lists or the term store, and users then generate new documents by pulling data from those sources or typing it in. Regular templates are static sample files without fields or data links and are included with Microsoft E3 and E5 licences. Modern templates require pay-as-you-go billing and permission to manage SharePoint lists, and through June 2026 a limited amount of content assembly was available at no cost to customers with pay-as-you-go billing set up. Limits: only Word files (.docx or .doc) are supported; the document cannot contain comments or have Track Changes switched on, and existing content controls must be removed; Smart Art and bulleted lists are not supported; a template is tied to one document library; and generated documents are not linked back to their template afterwards.

content-delivery-network.title: Content delivery network - Wikipedia
content-delivery-network.notes: A content delivery network (CDN) is a geographically distributed system of proxy servers and data centres. By placing servers closer to users it improves availability and speed. CDNs emerged in the late 1990s to relieve Internet bottlenecks and now deliver much of the Internet's content, including web pages, scripts, downloads, e-commerce and portal applications, live and on-demand video and social media. Content owners such as media companies and online retailers pay CDN operators to deliver their content, and CDNs in turn pay ISPs and network operators to host their servers. The term is broad and covers video streaming, software distribution, site acceleration, load balancing, performance measurement and analytics; some providers add security services such as DDoS protection and web application firewalls. Nodes are spread across many locations and networks, and large CDNs may run thousands of them. Requests are directed to the best node based on proximity, speed, server capacity or cost, using techniques such as caching popular content, load balancing and routing through DNS or anycast. The main benefits are lower bandwidth costs, faster page loads and greater global availability.

content-explorer.title: Learn about content explorer - Microsoft Purview
content-explorer.notes: Content explorer in Microsoft Purview shows a current snapshot of items in an organisation that carry a sensitivity label, carry a retention label, or match a sensitive information type. Items can be opened natively, the listing of the current view can be exported to CSV, and matches for sensitive information types or trainable classifiers can be marked Match or Not a Match to improve classifier accuracy. Encrypted documents cannot be previewed and downloads are disabled. Access has two tiers. Opening the tab needs a Compliance administrator, Security administrator or Compliance data administrator role, or one of the Information Protection roles or role groups. Viewing the items needs membership in the Content Explorer List viewer role group (see items and their locations) and/or the Content Explorer Content viewer role group (see item contents and names); the two are independent and administrative units can restrict them. Locations include Exchange, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive, and results can be filtered by mailbox address, site name, file name or extension.

conversational-boosting.title: Use generative answers / conversational boosting - Microsoft Copilot Studio
conversational-boosting.notes: Conversational boosting is a system topic that Copilot Studio creates by default when an agent is built. It contains a generative answers node, which lets the agent find and present information from knowledge sources without an author writing a topic for every question. Agent-level knowledge sources feed this node automatically, and generative answers nodes can also be placed inside individual topics so a search runs for specific intents and not just as a fallback. Supported knowledge sources include public websites (searched through Bing, limited to the sites specified), uploaded documents, SharePoint, Dataverse and enterprise data indexed through Microsoft Search connectors. SharePoint, Dataverse and connector sources use the agent user's Microsoft Entra identity, so answers only surface content that user can access. Limits depend on orchestration mode. In classic mode the topic caps sources by type, for example four website URLs, four SharePoint URLs, two Dataverse sources with up to 15 tables each and three custom data sources.

conways-law.title: Conway's law - Wikipedia
conways-law.notes: Conway's law holds that organisations tend to design systems whose structure mirrors their own communication patterns. The article credits the computer scientist and programmer Melvin Conway with introducing the idea in 1967, although the paper it cites dates from 1968. The reasoning is that components must fit together, so the people building them must communicate; where communication is difficult, social boundaries show up in the technical design, and complex products end up shaped like the organisations that made them. The page stresses that the law describes a correspondence and not a cause. Commentators disagree on the direction: some hold that technical design forces reorganisation, others that organisational structure dictates design, and others that both happen. Opinions on the phenomenon differ as well, with some seeing the mirroring as helpful, some as an undesirable organisational bias and some as a necessary compromise given human limits.

copilot-credit-pre-purchase-plan.title: Save on Copilot Credits with the pre-purchase plan - Microsoft Cost Management
copilot-credit-pre-purchase-plan.notes: The Copilot Credit Pre-Purchase Plan lets an organisation prepay for Copilot Credit usage at a discount. Customers buy commit units (CUs) in tiers, and larger purchases earn bigger discounts. Each plan has a one-year term, and Copilot Credit usage automatically draws down the CUs at a rate of 1 CU per 1 US dollar of retail cost until the term ends or the CUs run out. By default the plan renews automatically, and that setting can be changed. The page's example is a Tier 2 plan of 15,000 CU bought for 14,100 US dollars, which saves about 6 percent against 15,000 dollars at pay-as-you-go rates. Discounts do not stack with other discounts, so the effective saving may be smaller than the tier percentage. The scope can be a single resource group, a single subscription, shared (eligible subscriptions in the billing context, such as an EA enrollment) or a management group. After purchase the scope and the people who manage the reservation can be changed, but plans cannot be split or merged. Cancellations and exchanges are not supported, so purchases are final. Buying a plan requires the Owner or Reservation Purchaser role for an Azure subscription, the Reserved Instances policy enabled for an EA subscription, or the appropriate CSP arrangement.

copilot-grounding.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot architecture - Microsoft Learn
copilot-grounding.notes: This Microsoft Learn page treats grounding at a high level. Every Copilot experience combines large language models with grounding in web data, organisational data or both. Organisational data arrives through Microsoft Graph and Work IQ, and access always respects the signed-in user's permissions, with security and compliance controls enforced. What grounding is available depends on the licence. Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) and the usage-based billing experiences automatically retrieve web and work data through Microsoft Graph and Work IQ; users can point to specific files to focus on but do not have to upload them. Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) are grounded in public web data by default and cannot reach organisational data through Microsoft Graph. They can use organisational content only when a user uploads a file with a prompt, works with open content in Outlook or Teams, or uses a pay-as-you-go agent that has access to that content. For users signed in with Microsoft Entra accounts, Enterprise Data Protection covers prompts and responses, and EU traffic stays within the EU Data Boundary.

copilot-web-search.title: Manage web search in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat - Microsoft Learn
copilot-web-search.notes: Web search in Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat is an optional feature that lets Copilot pull in information from the web, through the Bing search service, to ground its answers in current data. Copilot builds a short search query from the user's prompt instead of sending the whole prompt, and it does not send Microsoft 365 files or Entra ID details. Users can see the exact queries in citations in Copilot Chat, and admins can audit them through eDiscovery and Purview. Microsoft commits that these queries are not used to improve Bing, build advertising profiles or train foundation models. Admins control the feature with the Allow web search in Copilot policy in the Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365. When enabled it offers three options: on in both Copilot and Copilot Chat, off in both, or off in Work mode but on in Web mode and Copilot Chat. If the policy is off, users cannot turn web search on. If it is not configured, web search is available by default, unless optional connected experiences in Office are disabled. For US government customers (GCC and DoD) web search is off by default and stays off unless the policy is configured. Users with web search allowed can switch it off with the Web content toggle in Copilot settings, a preference that persists across devices.

corporate-social-responsibility.title: Corporate social responsibility - Wikipedia
corporate-social-responsibility.notes: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) is a form of voluntary, self-regulated business practice in which companies run their core operations responsibly, to benefit society and the environment and to reduce harm. It covers ethical production, employment and investment. CSR often takes the form of philanthropy, volunteering or grants, but many firms now take a strategic approach that aligns social goals with their brand and stakeholders. Definitions vary widely depending on whether the speaker is a business leader, an activist or a government official. The triple bottom line, coined by John Elkington in 1994, is one way to evaluate it, weighing people (fair labour and community well-being), planet (sustainable environmental practices) and profit. Listed companies often report this through environmental, social and governance disclosures, and some countries require such reporting. Some studies link CSR to better financial and employee performance, though the average correlation is small, and reported benefits include stronger reputation, easier recruitment and retention and lower regulatory risk. India requires qualifying companies to spend 2 percent of profits on CSR activities.

cost-to-serve.title: Cost to serve - Wikipedia
cost-to-serve.notes: Cost to serve (CTS or C2S) is an accounting and financial-planning tool that measures how profitable it is to serve a particular customer account or customer type. It takes account of the actual business activities and overhead costs involved, which helps companies reshape how they serve customers in order to improve margins. Gartner describes it as an analysis that measures the profitability of products, customers and sales routes and supports decisions about service mix and operational changes for each customer. The Australian Food and Grocery Council calls it a general term for a rigorous method of estimating the likely financial results of supply chain investments and collaborative efforts. In supply chain management the tool shows how costs accumulate along the chain, since different products and customers require different activities and carry different cost profiles. Pareto analysis curves are often used to show which products and customers contribute most to profit and which erode it. Compared with activity-based costing, cost to serve needs fewer resources because it relies on broader analysis built on a mix of cost drivers.

critical-data-element.title: Critical data elements - Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog - Microsoft Learn
critical-data-element.notes: In the Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog, a critical data element (CDE) is a logical container, currently a preview feature, that groups the most important information in a data estate. Each CDE gathers related columns from different tables and assets. The page's example is a Customer ID element that brings together a CustID column from one table and a CID column from another, so users can match records across sources. Data producers can also use a CDE as a template for the expected format and quality of new assets. CDEs are created within governance domains and can have access policies applied to them, which helps organisations focus governance effort where it matters most. Creating CDEs and mapping columns requires data steward or data product owner permissions, and editing requires the data steward role. A domain must be published before its CDEs can be published, and other users see a CDE as a search filter only once it is published. Columns can be added or removed, glossary terms linked and custom attributes set; access policies apply to all associated data products. CDEs can be created individually or imported in bulk from a CSV file, which creates them as drafts, and bulk import cannot update existing elements.

cross-filter-direction.title: Create and manage relationships in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn
cross-filter-direction.notes: In Power BI Desktop a relationship's cross filter direction can be set to Single or Both. Single is the default and the most common choice: filters flow only from one table toward the table where values are aggregated. Models imported from Power Pivot in Excel 2013 or earlier use single direction for every relationship. Both treats the connected tables as one for filtering purposes, so filters flow in either direction. This suits a star schema, in which a central fact table connects to several lookup tables. The page's example counts employees per project: with single direction the count is the same on every row, because filters cannot travel from the project table up to the employee table, and setting the relationship to Both corrects the report. Both comes with cautions. If two fact tables share lookup tables, for instance sales and budget tables both linked to a department table, Both can create ambiguous filter paths and should be avoided, and Power BI blocks Both when it would create such ambiguity. The page suggests two remedies: deactivating or removing relationships to reduce loops, or importing a table a second time under a different name to turn the model into a star schema, where Both works safely.

csharp.title: C Sharp (programming language) - Wikipedia
csharp.notes: C# is a general-purpose, high-level programming language that supports several paradigms, including object-oriented, functional and imperative styles, with a syntax resembling other C-style languages. Anders Hejlsberg was the principal designer and lead architect at Microsoft, working with Scott Wiltamuth and Peter Golde, and the language was first widely distributed in July 2000. It was later standardised by Ecma in 2002 and by ISO/IEC in 2003, and the latest stable version listed is C# 14 from November 2025. Microsoft introduced C# together with the .NET Framework and Visual Studio, both initially proprietary, and the language maps closely to the Common Language Infrastructure. The open-source Mono project (2004) and Microsoft's own cross-platform tools, including the Roslyn compiler and the unified .NET platform, later widened its reach. Memory is garbage collected, and raw pointers are limited to blocks marked unsafe. The language offers classes, interfaces, generics (since version 2.0), properties, delegates, events and operator overloading; it does not allow multiple class inheritance, though a class can implement several interfaces, and it has no checked exceptions. Lambdas and LINQ brought functional features over time.

cuda.title: CUDA - Wikipedia
cuda.notes: CUDA is a proprietary parallel computing platform and programming interface from Nvidia. It lets software use Nvidia GPUs for general-purpose work beyond graphics, especially artificial intelligence, scientific research and high-performance computing. It began around 2004 as a project by Ian Buck, who had been developing a GPU programming language called Brook at Stanford; Nvidia hired him that year, and CUDA was publicly released in 2007. The platform includes drivers, runtime components, compilers, libraries and developer tools. A typical workflow copies data from main memory to the GPU, launches a compute kernel, lets the GPU's many cores run it in parallel and copies the results back, with threads running in groups of 32 called warps. Developers can write CUDA code in C and C++ and can also use Fortran, Python and Julia through bindings and libraries such as PyCUDA and CuPy; it also works alongside frameworks such as OpenMP, OpenACC and OpenCL. Several limits apply. CUDA runs only on Nvidia hardware, and its proprietary nature is the key difference from open alternatives such as AMD's ROCm and Intel's oneAPI.

customer-asset.title: Customer assets - Dynamics 365 Field Service - Microsoft Learn
customer-asset.notes: A customer asset in Dynamics 365 Field Service represents a piece of a customer's equipment that needs inspection, maintenance or repair. Each asset tracks its location and its service history, including all past and present work orders. Key fields are Name (required), Category, Product (linked to the product catalogue), Account (the service account for the customer and location), Functional Location and Parent Asset, which supports hierarchies such as a part inside a larger device; child assets are added in the Sub Assets grid. Assets can be created manually, imported in bulk from Excel (which needs Name and Account columns) or generated automatically: when a product is marked Convert to Customer Asset, completing or closing a work order that uses it creates one asset per work order product, whatever the quantity. Categories group assets and let property templates be applied to many assets at once. Assets are linked to work orders, and by default only assets tied to the work order's service account can be used, a behaviour that can be changed in settings. With Connected Field Service, sensors can be linked to an asset in a one-to-many relationship; IoT alerts tag the related asset, and a work order created from an alert includes both the alert and the asset.

dapr.title: Dapr - Wikipedia
dapr.notes: Dapr (Distributed Application Runtime) is a free, open-source runtime for cloud-native and serverless computing. Microsoft and Diagrid developed it, and the first release came in October 2019. It is written in Go, runs cross-platform and is licensed under Apache 2.0, having started under MIT, with the source hosted on GitHub. The article mentions Dapr's sidecar, a companion process that runs alongside an application, though it does not explain the design in depth. Applications reach Dapr through HTTP or gRPC APIs, and SDKs exist for Java, .NET, Python, Go, JavaScript and Rust. It can run on Kubernetes or on a local machine in self-hosted mode. Its building blocks include workflows, service-to-service invocation, publish and subscribe messaging, state management, bindings, actors, secrets, configuration, distributed locks, cryptography, jobs and conversation, which gives access to language model providers. The APIs are meant to be portable across clouds and hosting environments. Dapr is a CNCF project that graduated in November 2024. Its current focus is durable, verifiable execution so that workflows and AI agents survive failures and run to completion, and workflow history can be cryptographically signed to make it tamper-evident.

data-historian.title: Operational historian - Wikipedia
data-historian.notes: An operational historian, commonly called a data historian, is a time-series database application built for process data in manufacturing. It works alongside distributed control systems and PLCs to improve data capture, validation, compression and aggregation. Industries use historians for supervisory control, performance monitoring, quality assurance and machine learning on large volumes of past data. They originally captured instrumentation and control readings, which is why each data stream is called a tag, after the physical tags once attached to instruments for manual logging. Data can be retrieved through OPC HDA, SQL or REST API interfaces. Engineers and operators mainly use operational historians inside the plant for oversight and analysis; they record all instrumentation and control data, whereas enterprise historians store only a subset to support business functions. Vendors supply APIs and SDKs for fast reads and writes, and trending tools are the most common front ends. Because they sit close to the process equipment they are often marketed as real-time databases, although vendors trade off capture speed against analysis features differently.

data-management-framework.title: Data import and export jobs overview - Finance and Operations - Microsoft Learn
data-management-framework.notes: This page describes how the Data management workspace in Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations handles data import and export jobs, the core of the data management framework. Each job uses staging tables, which let data be verified, cleaned or converted before it moves to or from the target entity. Jobs follow a fixed sequence: define the job, map source and target columns, check security, run the job, review its history and clean up staging tables. Each job needs a file format (Excel, XML, or delimited or fixed-width) and should use a Unicode code page for consistent results. Entities are sequenced by execution unit, level and sequence; entities at the same level run in parallel and levels run in order. Jobs can be restricted by role, user or legal entity, and they can run in batch, which is recommended for large volumes, or immediately. Limits and constraints include: XML formats cannot contain illegal control characters; delimited data must not contain the chosen delimiter or qualifier; some entities, such as Vendors V2, must use an import task count of 1; and excessive parallel tasks can push resource use to 100 percent.

data-processing-agreement.title: Art. 28 GDPR - Processor
data-processing-agreement.notes: Article 28 of the GDPR sets out when and how a controller may use a processor, and so defines what a data processing agreement must contain. A controller may only use processors that provide sufficient guarantees of appropriate technical and organisational measures. The relationship must be governed by a binding written contract or other legal act under EU or Member State law, including in electronic form. It must set out the subject matter and duration of the processing, its nature and purpose, the types of personal data and data subjects, and the rights and obligations of the controller. The contract must require the processor to act only on the controller's documented instructions, to ensure its staff are bound by confidentiality and to apply security measures. The processor must also help the controller respond to data subject requests and meet obligations on security, breach notification, impact assessments and prior consultation. At the controller's choice, the processor must delete or return all personal data when services end, and it must provide information needed to show compliance and allow audits. If it believes an instruction breaches data protection law, it must say so immediately.

data-protection-addendum.title: Product Terms - Privacy and Security Terms (Data Protection Addendum) - Microsoft Licensing
data-protection-addendum.notes: This section of Microsoft's Product Terms explains how the Data Protection Addendum (DPA) applies. The DPA sets the rules for processing and securing data, and it prevails over conflicting terms in a customer's licensing agreement. It covers Customer Data, Professional Services Data and Personal Data handled by Microsoft products, though several products are excluded or modified; Bing Search, Web IQ and Grounding with Bing, for example, fall outside it, and some containerised or on-premises services run in environments Microsoft does not control. Roles differ by data type: Microsoft acts as a controller for certain data, such as Windows diagnostic data, Windows Server data and Internet-based features, and for those its Privacy Statement applies in place of the DPA. For Windows, Microsoft is a processor only when the customer sets the diagnostic data processor configuration. Core Online Services store Customer Data at rest in designated geographic areas, and EU and EFTA customers can use the EU Data Boundary, although some transfers outside it still occur, for example for remote support, security and customer-initiated actions.
